area: mac4DSTEM/Core/Analysis — disk detection, probe kernel, virtual detector, origin/ellipse/Q calibration
summary: The ported math in this area is unusually faithful and I could not break it. I checked `DiskDetection.findMaxima` line-by-line against `preprocess/utils.py:get_maxima_2D` — the mixed `>=`/`>` 8-neighbour tie-breaking is transposed correctly into the app's (x=column, y=row) frame, the filter cascade order and the brightest-first spacing walk are equivalent to `filter_2D_maxima`, `polyRefine` reproduces the parabolic offsets AND the bilinear intensity update py4DSTEM applies afterwards, and `MatrixDFTCorrelation.refine` performs both roundings (half-pixel, then 1/upsampleFactor) that `upsampled_correlation`'s docstring insists on, on the unsmoothed complex correlation exactly as `_ar_FT=cc` does. `ProbeKernel` matches `generate_synthetic_probe` and `get_probe_kernel_edge_sigmoid(type="sine_squared")` including the wrapped-coordinate convention; `EllipseCalibration.userParameters` is algebraically identical to `convert_ellipse_params` (I verified a=1/√λ₋ from py4DSTEM's b4a form), the Janus-Gaussian model matches `double_sided_gaussian` including the heaviside split, and `Calibration.ellipseTransform` is a literal transcription of `braggvectors.py:507-513`. `make_detector`'s circle/annulus predicates match. The three Metal parameter structs (`ApertureParams`, `CoMParams`, `OriginParams`) are byte-for-byte identical to their `.metal` counterparts, all 4-byte fields. `fitOriginTrimmed`, `QCalibrationRun` and `QCalibrationShellCheck` are exemplary: they record what was refuted, refuse to invent thresholds, and carry the position count as part of the claim. My findings are therefore mostly about claims that have drifted away from the code rather than about the numbers themselves — but one of them (finding 1) is precisely the shape of drift that has already caused a wrong "correction" in this repo once.

findings.title: Stale doc comment says the origin gate reads `robustResidual`; the code reads the full-scan RMS, and the swap was already refuted by Gate B
findings.why: `Calibration.swift:421-422` ends the `robustResidual` doc with "The gate reads this one deliberately — see `originFitIsSane`. // v2 S13". `originFitIsSane` (`Calibration.swift:569-571`) reads `origin?.rmsResidual` — the FULL-SCAN RMS — and the 40-line comment at `Calibration.swift:533-560` explains at length that S13 shipped the robust-residual version, Gate B refuted it with a measured counterexample (12×12 corner block thrown +40 px: keptResidual 9.94 passes, full-scan 15.64 blocks), and it was reverted. So lines 417-421 argue correctly against using `robustResidual`, and then line 422 asserts the opposite. The same reverted claim survives a second time at `mac4DSTEM/UI/CalibrationDetailsView.swift:52-55` ("the residual the GATE judged, which is the robust one where a robust fit ran") immediately above the `judgedOriginResidual` display, and a third time in `docs/open-items.md:504-505` ("the gate — renamed `originFitIsSane` — reads the **robust** residual"), which `docs/open-items.md:617` then contradicts. This is the exact failure CLAUDE.md records for 2026-08-27: a session found a paragraph disagreeing with a stub and resolved it the wrong way.
findings.failureScenario: A later session touches origin calibration, reads `robustResidual`'s doc comment at :422 (or the UI comment at CalibrationDetailsView.swift:53), concludes `originFitIsSane` has drifted off the intended statistic, and "fixes" it to `origin?.robustResidual`. That reinstates the exact defect Gate B measured: a scan with a spatially clustered quarter of failed origin positions is fitted 15.03 px off the true beam centre, `keptResidual` reads 9.94 against a 10.624 px probe radius, `originFitIsSane` returns true, `originSupportsReciprocalMetrology` passes, and `calibrateQFromCrystal` stamps a Q pixel size `.measuredInApp` derived from a 15 px-displaced origin — far past the ~2 px where the estimator's `minimumRadiusPixels` floor stops distinguishing the direct beam from the first shell.

findings.title: `KnownCrystalQCalibration.estimate` takes `probeRadiusPixels` and never reads it, while its doc promises a check that runs on it
findings.why: `probeRadiusPixels: Double?` is declared at `QCalibration.swift:119` and appears nowhere else in the file — `grep -c probeRadiusPixels QCalibration.swift` returns 2, the signature and the doc line. The doc at `QCalibration.swift:106-110` says both `secondShellRadiusInvAngstrom` and `probeRadiusPixels` are "**not optional-with-a-default on purpose**: a caller that cannot supply them gets an estimate whose checks silently did not run, and this repo's documented failure mode is exactly a check that was believed to have happened. Pass nil explicitly and the estimate says `.notSelfChecked`." That is true of the second-shell radius and false of the probe radius: `.notSelfChecked` is produced only at `:178` and `:180`, both from `expectedRatio` (i.e. `secondShellRadiusInvAngstrom`), and no code path consumes the probe radius. The parameter is the residue of `minimumShellRadiusRatioOfProbe = 1.0`, one of the three thresholds the same file's own comment block at `:70-99` records Gate B as having cut on 2026-08-28. The doc was not updated with the cut, so the file now promises a self-check it does not perform — and note `:96-98` separately records that the probe radius is over-measured 2.15×, i.e. a check on it would have been unsound anyway.
findings.failureScenario: `AppState.swift:5037` computes `probeRadiusPixels` from `calibration.probeRadius` and passes it at `:5056`; `tools/real-acom-benchmark/main.swift:101` and `tools/training-dataset-campaign/main.swift:771` pass the fitted probe radius too. A reviewer auditing what the Q estimator validates reads :106-110, sees a live probe-radius argument threaded from four call sites, and records that a shell radius implausibly small relative to the probe is caught. Nothing catches it. `tools/q-calibration-gate-test/main.swift:390,425,436` reinforce the illusion by passing `probeRadiusPixels: 5` in assertions that would pass identically with any value, including nil — the harness at :446 pairs `secondShellRadiusInvAngstrom: nil, probeRadiusPixels: nil` and attributes the resulting `.notSelfChecked` to both, when only the first argument produced it.

findings.title: `probeSize` uses `sorted[n/2]` where py4DSTEM uses `np.median`, an unmarked deviation in a file whose header promises every deviation is marked
findings.why: `OriginCalibration.swift:54-55` computes `let sorted = dr.sorted(); let median = sorted[n / 2]`. The default `n` is 100 (`:35`), so the array is even-length and this is the 51st order statistic, not the median. py4DSTEM's `get_probe_size` uses `np.median(dr_dtheta)` (`References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/calibration/probe.py:53`), which for even length averages the 50th and 51st. The value is then doubled into the acceptance criterion at `OriginCalibration.swift:59` (`dr[i] >= 2 * median`), so the discrepancy is doubled before it is used. The file header at `:10-11` states "All algorithms are ports of the py4DSTEM reference implementations; deviations are marked DEVIATION with a reason", and the very next branch at `:62-65` does carry a proper DEVIATION note for the empty-`trusted` fallback — so the omission here is a rule violation, not a stylistic gap. (Note the same even-length median is written correctly elsewhere in the same file, `OriginCalibration.swift:313-320`, and in `QCalibration.swift:196-202` and `EllipseCalibration.swift:515-521`, which makes this look like an oversight rather than a decision.)
findings.failureScenario: On a dataset where `dr(thresh)` is flat near its centre — a pattern with a broad plateau of intermediate thresholds, which is the normal shape for a well-exposed probe — the 50th and 51st sorted derivatives straddle the acceptance boundary. Doubling the wrong one shifts which threshold indices land in `trusted` at `:59`, and therefore both `r` (the mean of `rVals[trusted]`, `:67`) and `thresh` (`:68`, which sets the CoM mask). The app's probe radius then differs from py4DSTEM's `get_probe_size` on identical input, and the radius propagates into `ProbeKernel.synthetic`'s kernel scale, `DiskDetectionParams.detectorAdapted`'s `minPeakSpacing` and the `r * rscale` CoM window in `OriginMeasure.metal:74`. Any parity harness comparing the app's probe radius to py4DSTEM's is silently comparing two different estimators.

findings.title: Seven ellipse-fit refusal thresholds carry no derivation and no DEVIATION note, on a path py4DSTEM does not gate at all
findings.why: `fit1D` refuses on `maximumResidual: Double = 0.2` (`:79`), on angular occupancy below `angularBinCount / 3` of 36 bins with strong-pixel cut `minimum + 0.2 * dynamicRange` (`:122-123`, `:131`), and on shape bounds `b/a >= 0.2`, `a <= outerRadius * 1.5`, `b >= max(1, innerRadius * 0.25)` (`:213-215`); `fitBestAvailable` adds `maximumConicResidual = 0.2` / `maximumProfileResidual = 0.22` (`:240-241`); `fitAmorphousRing` adds `parameters[8] / parameters[9] <= 5` (`:496`). py4DSTEM's `fit_ellipse_1D` / `fit_ellipse_amorphous_ring` (`References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/calibration/ellipse.py:102`) impose none of these — they return whatever scipy converges to. The repo hard rule is "Port deviations from py4DSTEM get an inline `DEVIATION` note with the reason"; only the angular-coverage gate has any comment (`:120-121`, "stricter than scipy.leastsq"), and none of the eight constants has a stated derivation. This is the same class of decision that Gate B refuted three times on 2026-08-28 (`QCalibration.swift:70-99` records why: geometric centring is not invariant under reparametrisation, and the "sound" side of a gap has to be identified from data). Compounding it, `normalizedResidual` is documented at `:32` as one "dimensionless residual" but is `sqrt(Σ[(Adx²+Bdxdy+Cdy²−1)·I]² / ΣI²)` for `.conic` (`:214` region, computed at `:215`) and `sqrt(Σε²/N)/dynamicRange` for `.asymmetricGaussian` (`:493`) — two incommensurable statistics compared against the neighbouring 0.2 and 0.22.
findings.failureScenario: A low-dose or heavily-binned amorphous-halo pattern with a genuinely broad ring fits correctly but scores `normalizedResidual` 0.25. The app throws `FitError.excessiveResidual` and tells the user "Detector ellipse fit residual is too large (0.250)" (`:63`) with no way to tell whether 0.2 means anything, so a real elliptical distortion goes uncorrected and every downstream Bragg vector keeps it (`BraggVectors.calibrated` applies the ellipse matrix only when `hasEllipse`). In the opposite direction, a partial ring covering 12 of 36 sectors with a 4:1 axis ratio clears `b/a >= 0.2` and `a/b <= 5` and is accepted as a detector ellipse — which is exactly the degenerate case py4DSTEM's own `constrain_degenerate_ellipse` exists to warn about.
